description: AIT-ADS fox (Wazuh/Suricata), fenêtre étiquetée 'dnsteal' : une requête DNS vers un TLD inhabituel (.cloud) depuis l'hôte 172.17.130.196, des anomalies TLS impliquant une IP externe, et une tentative de connexion WordPress automatisée, noyées dans une majorité de connexions mail légitimes. Deuxième cas de référence d'investigation. Signal faible et bruit d'étiquetage (time_label) explicitement documentés ; aucune exfiltration n'est présentée comme confirmée.

reference_conclusion: Dans la fenetre etiquetee 'dnsteal' du testbed fox, la telemetrie Wazuh/Suricata contient une requete DNS vers un TLD inhabituel (.cloud) depuis l'hote 172.17.130.196 (signature Suricata 'ET INFO Observed DNS Query to .cloud TLD', severite faible), des anomalies TLS 'invalid handshake/record' entre l'hote interne 192.168.128.4 et l'IP externe 44.236.255.83, et une tentative de connexion WordPress automatisee (HeadlessChrome) dont le journal indique la meme IP source 172.17.130.196. Ces signaux justifient une ESCALADE pour investigation. Ils ne prouvent PAS une exfiltration de donnees : une seule requete DNS .cloud de faible severite et des anomalies TLS ambigues, sur un hote different de la requete DNS, ne demontrent ni le contenu eventuellement exfiltre, ni un lien causal entre les alertes DNS et TLS. La proximite temporelle dans une meme fenetre etiquetee n'etablit ni causalite ni attribution. La grande majorite des alertes de la fenetre (336 succes d'authentification Dovecot sur 381) sont des connexions mail legitimes, considerees ici comme du bruit benin issu de l'etiquetage temporel.
expected_unknowns: Le contenu eventuellement exfiltre n'est pas observable : une requete DNS vers un TLD .cloud ne revele ni donnee ni volume transfere.
Le lien entre les alertes DNS (172.17.130.196) et les anomalies TLS (192.168.128.4 vers 44.236.255.83) n'est pas etabli : il s'agit d'hotes internes differents.
La compromission eventuelle de l'hote 172.17.130.196 n'est pas demontree par ces alertes seules.
Le vecteur d'acces initial n'est pas present dans les preuves fournies.
Le caractere malveillant de la requete .cloud n'est pas confirme : .cloud est un gTLD legitime et une alerte 'ET INFO' est informationnelle, pas une detection d'exfiltration.
Le lien entre la tentative WordPress (e6) et l'activite DNS/TLS n'est pas etabli : seule l'IP source commune 172.17.130.196 est observee.

metadata.author: sentinelx
metadata.source_dataset: AIT Alert Data Set (Zenodo 8263181), fox testbed, Wazuh source
metadata.label_provenance: time_label: alerts are labeled 'dnsteal' only because their timestamp falls in the attack window of labels.csv. The per-event event_label is NOT distributed in this Zenodo record. See data/manifests/ait-ads.json.
metadata.label_confidence: LOW. Unlike the privesc window, this window is dominated by benign activity: 336 of 381 alerts are Dovecot IMAP login successes (benign mail). The exfiltration-relevant signal is a SINGLE low-severity Suricata 'ET INFO' DNS alert. Causal certainty is NOT established; the time_label marks a window, not a confirmed exfiltration.
metadata.window_composition: Source window = 381 alerts: 336 Dovecot authentication-success (rule 9701, benign mail logins = noise), 17 Suricata-alert summaries (rule 86601), 17 IDS full-log (rule 20101), 10 ClamAV database-update (rule 52507, benign), 1 WordPress login attempt (rule 31509). This scenario is a CURATED SUBSET of 10 real alerts and must NOT be presented as the full window.
metadata.genuine_signal: The DNS-exfiltration-relevant signal is a single Suricata event emitted as a pair: 'ET INFO Observed DNS Query to .cloud TLD' (rule 20101 level 6 full-log = e1, plus rule 86601 level 3 summary = e2) from 172.17.130.196:35954 -> 172.17.128.1:53 at 09:08:00.
metadata.paired_events: e1/e2 are the SAME Suricata DNS alert reported by two Wazuh rules (20101 full-log + 86601 summary). e3/e5 similarly pair a 20101 TLS full-log alert with its 86601 summary. They are counted once analytically, not as independent detections.
metadata.distinct_endpoints: The DNS .cloud query originates from 172.17.130.196; the TLS 'invalid handshake/record' anomalies are between internal host 192.168.128.4 and external 44.236.255.83:443 - a DIFFERENT internal host. No causal link between the DNS and TLS alerts is established; temporal co-occurrence in one labeled window is not evidence of a single activity.
metadata.shared_source_ip: The WordPress login attempt (e6) log shows source IP 172.17.130.196 - the same host as the DNS .cloud query - via automated HeadlessChrome and a POST /wp-login.php returning 302. This single-host co-occurrence is worth investigating but is NOT proof that the WordPress and DNS activity belong to one campaign.
metadata.attack_candidates: HYPOTHESES only, NOT confirmed: T1071.004 (Application Layer Protocol: DNS) and T1048 (Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol). Technique IDs/names verified against official MITRE ATT&CK pages (attack.mitre.org, 2026-10-22). A single low-severity DNS 'ET INFO' alert to a legitimate gTLD does not confirm either technique.
metadata.expected_techniques_rationale: expected_techniques is intentionally EMPTY: no ATT&CK technique is confirmed by this telemetry alone. The observed facts are an anomalous-TLD DNS query and TLS anomalies; mapping them to exfiltration or DNS C2 would be an inference, not an observation. Candidate techniques are documented in attack_candidates as hypotheses.
metadata.schema_limitation: Scenario.expected_techniques is a flat list without observed/inferred/not-demonstrated semantics; here it is empty and the observed-vs-hypothesis distinction is documented in metadata.
metadata.scope_limitation: All 10 curated events are provided upfront in alert.events, so this scenario tests interpretation under label noise and a weak signal, NOT tool-based retrieval.
metadata.not_a_benchmark: Second reference case grounded in AIT data; not a scientific benchmark nor a validation of SENTINEL-X.
